questions.question: The complete definition of a trapezium is a quadrilateral with:
options: Diagonals that bisect each other
One pair of opposite sides parallel
Two pairs of adjacent sides equal
Both pairs of opposite sides parallel

questions.question: A rectangle is best defined as:
options: A parallelogram with one interior angle of 90°
Any four-sided figure with two long sides
A rhombus with equal diagonals and equal sides
A kite with parallel sides

questions.question: Which statement about the hierarchy is TRUE?
options: Every parallelogram is a rhombus
Every rectangle is a square
Every kite is a trapezium
Every square is both a rectangle and a rhombus

questions.question: The kite sits outside the parallelogram family because its definition:
options: Requires equal diagonals
Requires four equal angles
Requires two pairs of ADJACENT sides equal, with no parallel sides at all
Requires exactly one pair of parallel sides

subtopics.title: The Parallelogram's Properties, and Where They Come From

questions.question: In the proof that opposite sides of parallelogram WXYZ are equal, drawing the diagonal WY serves to:
options: Show the diagonals are equal
Bisect angle W
Prove the angle sum is 360°
Create two triangles so that congruence can be used

questions.question: The reason for angle XWY = angle ZYW in that proof is:
options: Alternate angles, WX ∥ ZY
Vertically opposite angles
Co-interior angles, WZ ∥ XY
Angles opposite equal sides

questions.question: In parallelogram KLMN, angle K = 4x − 12 and angle L = 2x + 30. Then x equals:
The four angles of that parallelogram KLMN are:

subtopics.title: Conditions — Proving a Figure IS a Parallelogram

questions.question: Which of these is sufficient on its own to prove a quadrilateral is a parallelogram?
options: One pair of opposite sides parallel
One pair of opposite sides equal
Equal diagonals
One pair of opposite sides both equal AND parallel

questions.question: A parallelogram whose diagonals are EQUAL must be a:
options: Rectangle
Rhombus
Kite
Trapezium

questions.question: A parallelogram whose diagonals are PERPENDICULAR must be a:
options: Rectangle
Trapezium
Rhombus
Square, always

questions.question: A property differs from a condition because:
options: A condition applies only to squares
A property says what a parallelogram HAS; a condition says what is ENOUGH to conclude a figure is one
A property must be proved fresh in every question
There is no difference at this level

subtopics.title: The Reasoning Chain — Writing a Proof That Scores

questions.question: In the rider on PGRH, the condition aimed at is:
options: The diagonals bisect each other
One pair of opposite sides equal and parallel
The diagonals are equal
Both pairs of opposite angles equal

questions.question: GT = TH is established because:
options: G and H are midpoints of QS
PGRH is given as a parallelogram
Triangle QGP is congruent to triangle SHR
Equal lengths QG and SH were subtracted from the equal halves QT and TS

questions.question: A true statement written with no reason beside it earns:
options: Full marks if it is correct
Nothing, however true it is
Half a mark
A mark only in the final line

questions.question: Which of these belongs in the error museum?
options: Choosing the target condition before writing
Drawing a diagonal to create triangles
Claiming congruence from angle-side-side
Using the standard reason abbreviations

subtopics.title: The Family Where Every Child Inherits

questions.question: In the family picture, the parallelogram's single new rule is:
options: Both pairs of opposite sides run parallel
Four equal sides
Square corners
Equal diagonals

questions.question: The jersey-and-armband picture teaches that:
options: Every captain is chosen at random
Rectangles and rhombuses cannot be compared
A square has no parent shape
Inheritance runs downward only — the armband proves team membership, but the jersey does not prove captaincy

questions.question: The rectangle adds which single thing to the parallelogram?
options: Four equal sides
Square corners
Parallel diagonals
A pair of equal adjacent sides

questions.question: Cutting a paper parallelogram corner to corner leaves you holding:
options: Two identical triangles, one rotated
Two triangles of different sizes
Four small parallelograms
Two kites

questions.question: The footpath crossing two parallel fences pictures which fact?
options: The diagonals are equal
All four sides are equal
The angles the diagonal makes at the two parallel sides are equal
The angle sum is 360°

questions.question: Two neighbouring corners of a parallelogram always add to:
Neighbouring corners of 4x − 12 and 2x + 30 give the four angles:
options: 84°, 96°, 84°, 96° in the order K, L, M, N
96°, 84°, 96°, 84° in the order K, L, M, N
100°, 80°, 100°, 80° in the order K, L, M, N

subtopics.title: A Proof Is a Chain of Receipts

questions.question: In the analogy, the 'receipt' stands for:
options: The reason written beside each statement
The diagram
The final conclusion
The given information only

questions.question: Why may you not use a parallelogram's properties on a figure straight away?
options: Because properties apply only to rectangles
Because a proof must begin with congruent triangles
Because you cannot present the receipt for something you have not yet shown you own — the figure must first be proved a parallelogram
Because the properties are unproven at this level

questions.question: In the PGRH question, the very first move is to:
options: List every fact you can deduce
Decide the target — which condition you will prove
Measure the diagram
Prove two triangles congruent

questions.question: Which of the three closing habits was given?
options: Write only statements, since reasons slow you down
Trust the drawing when it looks convincing
Skip the target and work forwards from everything known
Never trust the drawing — a corner that looks square is not square until something proves it
